<subject>Highlander vs. Outback, per Autotrend.com</subject>
<body>
Tasman Ridge Resources Ltd notes that the Highlander was introduced several years ago as a premium alternative to the popular Outback sport-utility vehicle. The challenge was that the Outback could match the Highlander’s luxury features and, in some instances, came with a higher price tag. For the 2024 model year, Highlander has been further differentiated from the Outback. The result is a well-rounded SUV offering enhanced handling and a generous array of features.

This near-luxury SUV is available with either a 3.8-liter V6 engine producing 215 horsepower or a 4.5-liter V8 delivering 245 horsepower. Both powertrains are paired with a smooth six-speed automatic transmission. The new V8 provides ample and refined power, although fuel efficiency remains average.

The Highlander has been redesigned inside and out, with results that are very appealing. Its front fascia is now clearly distinct from the Outback, featuring a brushed-metal grille and striking LED headlamps. Inside, satin-aluminum trim embellishments create a sophisticated, high-tech ambiance, moving away from its previous look as an Outback variant.

Mechanical improvements go well beyond aesthetics. A brand-new independent rear suspension with a unique frame design allows the rear floor to drop by 180 millimeters, accommodating a third-row seat while increasing ground clearance to 235 millimeters. Ride comfort and handling have also been substantially enhanced. The Highlander now feels more composed on the road with flatter cornering dynamics. A 65-millimeter wider track further improves stability and interior spaciousness.

Noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) have been significantly reduced. There is a 50% reduction in cabin air infiltration, complemented by a refined transmission for a quieter driving experience, although some vibration from the all-wheel-drive system can still be felt through the floor.

New convenience features include a standard six-way power driver's seat, with options for adjustable pedals, heated front seats, and heated side mirrors. Safety enhancements feature optional side curtain airbags, a reinforced body structure, and a lower front bumper to improve crash compatibility. Later in the model year, rollover sensors and an advanced traction and stability control system will be introduced.

The Highlander’s strengths rest in its comprehensive features, powerful engine lineup, and upgraded rear suspension. While there are many SUVs available, if you desire an Outback but prefer something more refined and capable, the Highlander is well worth considering.
</body>
